utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a note for the transcript. We are interrupting the examination of (redacted) -- I'm sorry, of a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: 84 and taking -- the Prosecutor is now calling Dr. De Grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Doctor, would you please stand up and take the solemn declaration in the form in which the card the usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Groome. Examined by Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. De Grave, could you briefly describe your educational background for the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: I started as a civil -- [Interpretation] I started as a civil engineer and then I switched to medicine. I practised general medicine until about the 1980s. I'm interrupting my answers to allow the interpreters to do their job. If you say I should continue. I will continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: So as I was saying, I was engaged in general practice until the 1980s, then I was called as an expert by the tribunals, first for very minor cases and later on more and more important ones. I taught neurology, courses in neurology for three years, and up to now I have six different diplomas, the last being in criminal law and forensic medicine --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you called -- been called to serve as an expert to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: -- issued by the University of Gent. Not explicitly. I was asked whether I would be willing to do expert findings as an expert of the Tribunal. I never considered myself to be such, but when I'm asked something by whoever, I answer to the best of my abilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how many times have you rendered expert opinions for the Courts of Belgium?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: In general terms, one submits findings in writing to tribunals and I would say that on the average, I receive two and a half missions per week by tribunals and also other requests regarding opinions or arbitration for tribunals. Again, these come several times a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to today, have you been asked to render your medical expertise before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes. I was invited for a previous case, that is I was an expert, together with an expert from Serbia, Djukic. This is my second testimony here in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what experience you have regarding the examination and comparison of radiological X-rays?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: In my daily work, it is customary that we are given X-rays to look at the protocols. This is a classical method. In other cases, there are files covered by medical confidentiality, so you are given X-rays without any additional information. And one learns to read X-rays without the accompanying protocols. This develops the ability to be able to study, read and interpret X-rays but also to be able to judge the quality and occasionally, also the technique used to take those X-rays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you in the past been called upon to give your expertise on the interpretation of X-rays and the comparison of X-rays?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: This is a -- my daily occupation. Would I say that I am able to say that most disputes have to do with movement and that there are hardly no legal cases without X-rays, which always need to be interpreted, and an expertise consisting exclusively of X-rays is rare, but generally speaking, it is only a part of my work required when my expert opinion is requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last year were you asked to provide your medical expertise in connection with this case, the Prosecutor against Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was asked to take into consideration the case of Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic, and I was asked to take X-rays to compare with those that were brought to me. The first point was that I realised that I was facing X-rays of different persons. There was no similarity and therefore no way of comparing them. And I submitted my conclusions in an initial, a first, report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you asked to compare an X-ray purported to have been taken in 1992 with one that was taken in the detention facility here in Holland?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Indeed, I was asked to compare those X-rays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given an X-ray plate that bore the name of Mitar Vasiljevic and the date 14th of June 1992, by an investigator, Yves Roy, of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes, I received from Mr. Yves Roy two X-rays to compare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I'm wondering why we are worried about the X-rays taken last year, despite the doctor's rather confident assertion that he was facing X-rays of different persons, he went on to criticise the quality of the X-ray. That's why a second one was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking him about the X-ray from 92 at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm a little worried that we are stuck in last year's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I assure the Court we are not and I'm going to confine myself to the X-ray taken just recently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been in custody of -- for the remainder of your testimony, I'd ask you to refer to this X-ray that you were given from 1992 as the 1992 X-ray. And I would ask you, have you been in custody of that X-ray plate since the time you were given it to -- it was given to you by investigator Roy? Have you been in custody of that X-ray since the time it was given to you?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes. I was given two X-rays. There was this one. Can I show it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only X-ray that you were given by Mr. Roy that I will refer to, is the X-ray that says Mitar Vasiljevic, 14th of June 1992. And that is the one you have in your hand, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender that X-ray as Prosecution number 151?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P151.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, on the 15th of August this year, did you conduct an examination of Mr. Vasiljevic yourself?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes. I did carry out an examination of Mr. Mitar. I spoke to him. I questioned him. I examined him. I was assisted by Dr. Bollen for some new X-rays and radioscopy and what I have here before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. As part of that examination, were new X-rays taken of the leg of Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: We tried to make new X-rays with the same incidents as those that I have here on the ELMO, and I have my finger on it. And then we made this X-ray. I don't know if you can see it well but any way, these are X-rays and photos that I added to my report. There is also a difference here because, on the X-rays that -- the new X-rays we did, all these new X-rays confirm an element which makes them reconcile -- recognisable, name and date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. De Grave, I want to ask you, it sounds as if you took many X-rays, did you attempt to position the leg of Mr. Vasiljevic in such a way as to obtain an X-ray that was most suitable for comparison with the 1992 X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to put the other X-rays away and just take out the X-ray plate of the position of Mr. Vasiljevic that is most similar to the X-ray plate from 1992.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: They are these. In order to compare them, these are the two, and in profile, we have this X-ray.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So there are two X-rays that best simulate the position that a leg was in in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I would ask at this time that those X-rays be marked as Prosecution number 21, and I would tender them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Why have we got the wildly varying numbers, Mr. Groome, 21 and 151.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's just the numbering system that the -- the order in which they were originally conceived to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So there are two X-rays and they were taken in 2001: Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, August 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They will be Exhibit P21. Now for our own purposes, because what we see on the ELMO is absolutely nothing, could we have a reference to the pagination of the doctor's report which has reproduced various X-rays in colour for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I'd ask you maybe just put the other X-rays aside for the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've given the court deputy copies of the report. Would the Court like them handed up or is the Court already in possession of the doctor's report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I was hoping you were going to get the evidence without the content of the report because, as I mentioned to you yesterday, it is not expressed in the most helpful way. But the annexes to it, will be very helpful because we can then work from these rather than try to see something on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So I'd ask that they now be passed to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [In English] One more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, I would like to know which two of these plates consist of copies of Exhibit 21.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I'd ask you to take a look at a copy of your report which is being handed to you and take a look at document number 35, a photocopy of your original report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but you're talking about some document 35 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's the document I've just handed up to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to please refer us to the page of what we are now going to refer to as the 1992 X-ray. Is there a photograph or a reproduction of that X-ray plate in your report and, if so, tell us what page number.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: I have been given my second report and the original photographs were attached to my first report dated the 27th of March, and there, there is an original copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask to you place that on the ELMO. I believe we will be able to see that clearly on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm a little puzzled by the doctor's answer. He gave us a report last year, 2000. That report was, I thought, made before the X-rays were taken again this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He's talking about the 1992 X-ray at this time, Your Honour, which he's saying now he did not include in the report you have before you now, but in his original report. He has a very good reproduction of it here now that we will be able to see on the ELMO and I would propose that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That will be a copy of Exhibit 151, this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I had asked about Exhibit 21. We will get to that eventually, will we?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. This one is Exhibit 151. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the X-ray that you took on the 15th, or that was taken on the 15th of August 2001, can we from this point forward refer to that as the 2001 X-ray. And would I ask to you refer to the page on your report where a reproduction of that X-ray is contained.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: All the plates were reproduced in the annex to my report. On page 12 is a detail of the X-ray, of the heel. On page 13 is a comparison of the fractures. Page 14 are photos which can be compared with the photos of 1992, the X-rays. And the other photos are control X-rays, page 16 is to note that there were no ulterior fractures. Page 17 are general variations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, so is it true that the X-ray that is now Prosecution Exhibit number 21 is reproduced on page 14 of your report? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question for me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What we want to know, doctor, is where we will find a copy, a reproduction of the two X-rays which you have identified and which have become Exhibit 21. I think they are on the ELMO next to you. We want to see them in a document that we can follow. On what page of your latest report will we find those reproduced?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor we can not see the X-ray itself on the ELMO. I would ask you to place your reproduction of Exhibit number 21 on the ELMO side by side with the reproduction of the 1992 X-ray. Can you place both of those on the ELMO next to each other?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Wait a moment, Mr. Groome. I'm sorry. I don't think that we have still got an answer to the question I'm trying to seek. There were two X-rays, as I saw it, that became Exhibit 21. Now the document on page 14 that the doctor has referred to seems to be one X-ray, not two. There were two separate x-rays.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll see if I can clear that up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor on page 14 of your report, you're holding up now the original of document or Exhibit number 21. On that are two impressions or two exposures of an X-ray; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Was there not another what I would call a half sheet that the doctor had?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this is, what you're holding up in your hand, the most suitable X-ray taken in August of 2001 for comparison with the X-ray taken in 1992? Is that the most suitable one for comparison? Okay, answer yes or no, please?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. [In English] It's the best one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it contain two exposures of the leg?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, clearly it does, but Mr. Groome what I want to know is Exhibit 21 only that one sheet of X-ray with two exposures on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Okay. As long as we've got it clear because there was another half sheet, if I can say, that was floating around and I thought the doctor had held them up together. It may be that he was holding the 1992 X-ray up as well. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, if you could follow my instructions as far as the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: This is the 1992 X-rays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, would you please place the reproduction of the 1992 X-ray on the ELMO. Can you place that on the ELMO next to -- can you place it along side of the reproduction of the 2001 X-ray.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask the technician if it's possible to zoom out to take in both of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, did you compare the 1992 X-ray with the 2001 X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I was able to compare them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, let me ask you a few questions regarding them. Did you compare the fibula or small bone of the lower leg in those two X-rays? Did you compare those two bones?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes, I compared them. One shouldn't forget that it is not as easy to reproduce photographs but we can see on the photographs, but I also have the original X-rays. It is possible to see that the fibula is intact. There are no fractures, and here, this fibula is deformed on the outside, and the inside of the bone is also different. So I also have the original X-rays that confirm the differences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor --

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: This is the fibula.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment, because this has to be able to be read later. The deformed one to which you refer, doctor, that you're pointing to, that was in the 2001 X-ray, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 2001. And this one is 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, but doctor, when you say "here" and "here," that's all that comes down on the transcript. We want to be able to read this later and understand what it is you're talking about. Now, you said you compared the two fibulas. The 1992 fibula was not injured in any way, but the 2001 fibula is deformed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I would ask you to take the pen in front of you and write 1992 on the reproduction that represents the 1992 X-ray. There is a pen on the table in front of you.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask to you write 2001 on the other X-ray. Doctor, I would just ask you to take a look at what you marked on the X-ray closest to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm afraid the doctor has got the wrong year. It's 1982 he's written it should be 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to write 1992 on the X-ray or the reproduction on your left. Now I would ask you on the X-ray or the reproduction of the X-ray 2001 X-ray, would you please circle the deformity that you're now referring to?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you please circle the same area on the 1992 X-ray which does not indicate the same deformity?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, did you also examine the tibia or large bone of the lower leg?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes. I also examined the tibia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for us your findings regarding your comparison of the large bone in the 1992 X-ray and that of the 2001 X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: We also have other X-rays which can explain or confirm this. Let's take the 1992 one. There is a fracture which starts here and goes up to here, so at an angle as you can see, like this. Also, from the take in front, you have the top point and the lowest point in this direction. If you look at the fracture in 1992, it is spiral in form, a fracture, which is usually provoked in football, whose leg is fixed by the heel and then he does a pirouette. This is a fracture that one frequently finds among skiers, ladies walking in the street with a high heels which get caught between the stones. If we look at the fracture of 2001, but you can see that better on another X-ray, that we have here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you move any X-ray I'd like to ask you a few questions on the X-ray?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before you go, the doctor has made a very good point. When you asked him to select the X-rays which most -- which best provide a comparison, the 1992 one on the left is clearly a side-on view and not a head-on view whereas the two that we see in the document marked 2001 appear even to me to be head-on views. So can we have one or the other annexes to his report, because he's obviously got one there, which has a side-on view with which we can compare the 1992 X-ray on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll do that. I just want him to mark a few --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before you do it, though, can we just get the exhibits correct and then we can let the doctor -- because he wants to refer to a number of different ones to demonstrate the alterations. And I think we should have them all in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reproduction that's on the right that you've marked the deformity in the fibula, I would just ask to you write the number 1 on the bottom of that. We will call this the first X-ray that you're referring to in your testimony. Would you please write the number one on the bottom of that X-ray on the right.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is there another X-ray that you took which you think is more suitable for comparison of the large bone or tibia of the leg? Please Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. answer yes or no for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: For the fibula that you asked me about a moment ago, you have here a side-on view, this one, because this is the left leg and the right leg, and here again, left and right. And on the fibula, the question you put to me a moment ago, you can see here that the discontinuity. It was cracked like this and like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we have the number of the page in your report? It's not sufficiently clear I'm afraid, doctor, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, what page in the annex is this new X-ray that you're showing us now?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: 15, page 15. All the pages have been numbered. Page 15. One cannot make a mistake. All the reproductions have been numbered so as not to be confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We cannot read the number on the foot of the document you've got there. That's why I asked you. Now you've told us it's 15. That's all we want to know for the moment. Now, can we have this marked in some way as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm going to ask that the first one that he's referred to which bears the mark 2001 and has number 1 circled, that be tendered into evidence as 21.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That will change the number from 21 to 21.1. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, before you make any marks on the plate, I want to ask you to put 2001 on the bottom. I see you've done that and I would ask, Your Honour, that this document be marked as Prosecution or tendered as Prosecution Exhibit 21.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit P21.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, before you make any marks on it, I'm going to ask to you return to the 1992 X-ray and I'm going to ask you to draw a horizontal line to indicate the lowest -- where the fracture at its lowest point is on the leg. Where did the fracture end on the lowest part of the leg? Can you draw it with the blue pen, please, on the 1992 X-ray. On the 1992 X-ray.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Doctor, you're marking it on the wrong one. See the one which has 1992? Yes.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would I also ask you to mark the upper-most portion of the fracture. Okay. And I would ask you to draw a line parallel to the fracture to indicate the angle at which the fracture occurred --

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- on the 1992 X-ray.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: To answer your question, on page 13 of my report, you can find the various angles of the X-rays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: The diagram. Of the fracture in 1992, there is a line indicating it. The direction of the fracture that I X-rayed on the 15th of August goes along this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that page 13 of the annex be marked or tendered as Prosecution Exhibit 21.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's page 13. Right, any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Unfortunately the documents that I was given, at least the copies of the documents I was given, it's marked page 11 of 11 but it's obviously the same document. That will be Exhibit P21.3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor I would ask you just to point out with the pointer the angle of the fracture that you observed on the 1992 X-ray. On page 13 of your annex.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Here it is. This is one angle. And one needs to have what school children have, to measure the angle. Regarding the question of angle, these are angles. This is a method to calculate the angle relying on the X-ray. To have the real angle, one needs to have three dimensions. But this shows the whole layout. In medicine we don't talk about angles but about a plane, which is horizontal, so to speak. Based on the X-rays that I took on the 15th of August, you see a direction that is almost vertical, but I would -- I did not speak of angles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to place your pen along side and leave it for a moment, along the plane of the fracture that you observed in the 2001 X-ray. And now would you shift the pen to parallel the angle of the 1992 X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd ask that you take 21.3 off the ELMO now at this point. Would you remove page 13 of your report from the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, despite the preference of the doctor for the word plane, I'm not quite sure that I understand what it means other than the angle. Is it just a technicality, doctor, or can a layman describe that as the angle through the bone at which the fracture has gone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, doctor, but we are getting no translation at all. You'll have to start again, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Your Honour. I failed to switch on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Could you give us the description again or the explanation again, doctor, I'm sorry, but the translators didn't have their microphone on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you go to a butcher and who takes his axe and he's going to cut a piece of meat along a certain line, but in this case, it's as if you take a branch of a tree, you put it on your knee and you break it. In that case, you have a surface which is irregular. But the general impression is it gives you a certain direction, a certain inclination. It's like a piece of ground that you look at and you say that it is slopey or hilly or it has an angle of ten degrees. It is a piece of raised ground. If you go to Switzerland, you climb the mountains, you see a crevice which is almost vertical, but it is difficult to measure the degree. You would have to measure it and it would be between zero and 90 degrees. So that is why I don't talk about degrees because this can only provoke dispute. We talk about a plane. If you look at the leg, you look at the average inclination or direction of the fracture. I hope I have managed to explaining myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How about the expression, general direction, so that the general direction of the 1992 fracture is as shown in your document. And the general direction of the fracture that is shown in the 2001 X-ray is as shown in your document? Would that be a fair enough use of the words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is an approximate approach.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask that page 13 of the doctor's report be removed from the ELMO. Perhaps if the usher could assist the doctor in just organising the remaining documents so that we can see them. Just page 13, if page 13 is removed. I would ask that the reproduction on the ELMO -- we just had the reproduction of the 1992 X-ray and page 15 of the doctor's annex, the profile of the leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I would ask to you place your pen to show the angle of the fracture on the X-ray itself, just as you did on page 13. Would you please place your pen on the 1992 X-ray parallel to the fracture? Just place your pen on the X-ray and leave it there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask to you place the pen, leave the pointer where it is, place the pen to show us the plane of the fracture on the 2001 X-ray. Page 15 of your report.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've just drawn a line. Is that to indicate the upper-most portion of the fracture?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: This is the upper part and the lower part, the superior and interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, in addition to examining the tibia and the fibula or the large and small bone of the lower leg, did you also examine and compare the structures of the heel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are we going to go back to the length of the fractures? Because as I understand it, the doctor thinks that that is very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, before we leave the fracture of the Tibia and fibula, I want to ask you one additional question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is the tibia you mean, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The tibia. The large bone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to measure the length of the fractures?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: This is also to be found on the diagram and I measured the length of the fracture at this point. This was the fracture. It starts there and stops here. Which means that it starts at the superior point up here and it stops there. You can see it on the photograph. So the elements allow us to localise the two points, as I have indicated here, which gives you the length of the fracture. This hasn't been properly calculated. Just one moment. The other fracture goes from here. I can now see that the indications have slipped but there you have the two elements. No. I apologise. I seem to be having trouble myself now, getting my bearings. This is the first fracture, the top of it, and it goes down to the bottom here. And the other is from here to here. It's very difficult to do this on a photograph. This is the inferior point down here. The measurements were for another version, because at the beginning I was a little worried about the fact and troubled by the fact that we didn't think that the photographs were comparables. That is why I added in my report this other study. So this is the effect of different apparatuses and different moments and conditions under which the X-rays were taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, let me ask you a few questions. Given this variability that you're now telling us about, given what you're saying is possible uncertainty, are you able to say or are you able to accurately compare the length of the fractures?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What the doctor has already said is that this diagram that is 21.3 was compiled by reference to the earlier, that the 2000 X-rays, and therefore he is not satisfied it is accurate. But what I would like, if we can, from the doctor, is to, by reference to the 2001 X-rays and the 1992 X-rays, is he able to tell us what the difference in the length of the fracture is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to answer that question, doctor?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: The exact length was measured. It was 20 centimetres, 3 millimetres. It goes from there to there, 20.3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which X-ray are you talking about, doctor, the X-ray taken in 2001?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: 2001, yes. They were 90 -- as regards my second report, I am dealing with the 15th of August 2001. So the first report includes all the X-rays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Look, doctor, please, do not tell us details from your first report because you yourself concede that they are not likely to be accurate. What I want to know, and it's very important, as I understand it, from having read your report, is that the length of the fracture shown in the most recent X-rays is a different length to that which is shown in the 1992 X-rays. And what I want to obtain from you is your assessment of what the lengths are. Now I understanding you to have said that the 2001 X-ray shows the length of the fracture as being 20.3 centimetres. What does the 1992 X-ray show it to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 15 centimetres. 15.2, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you able -- you've been drawing little lines. Are you able on the documents we have now got, the reproductions of the two X-rays, or three X-rays, to show us where you find those marks? Now, in the 1992 one, let's take that one first, the one with the grids across it. You seem to have drawn a line on the left-hand side of the bone on one. Just take it -- that's right. Now you see -- yes, that's one mark there, and you have another mark up on the top on the right-hand side of the bone next to the fibula. You see where you've drawn that line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The figure I used to trace this was this one here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please, doctor, just would you just answer my question? We will get along a lot more quickly if you do. On that document which you've now got your right hand on, you have drawn a line on the left-hand side of the bone, just where one of those grids goes across, it and you've drawn another line, so far as I can see, on the right-hand side of the bone, somewhat higher up. Can you see where you've done that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One should always take, in order to compare and to answer your question, the extreme points. Here the extreme point is the superior one up here and the second extreme point is the inferior or lower point there. So the upper and lower. So those two points are reproduced on this diagram; that is to say, the two points on this diagram represent the plane of the fracture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Doctor, I still want to know what the mark is on the right-hand X-ray there, of the 1992 document. You drew two lines. You've pointed one of -- to one of them just then. And you can follow up -- no, no, look. Just take the one where your pen is now pointing towards. Go to the right-hand side of it. I think the usher has got his finger very close to it. Now, can you follow up a line that appears to be the fracture in that bone? So that on the fibula side of it, there is another line which I saw you draw, and I want to know what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the fracture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no, doctor. It's the one next to it, on the right-hand side of it. You see the one that's the head-on view? Yes. Now, that's right. Is that the fracture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So the line you had drawn on the right-hand side of it is the top of the fracture? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And is that the 15.2 centimetres that you've given us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We are getting no interpretation again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [English] You see I'm troubled on the [Interpretation] I see that I'm not quite clear on the numbers with regard to millimetres and centimetres but actually I can reproduce what we see on the right-hand side, starting from the extreme points, these four points, in order to measure the maximum size of the fractures. We are now discussing measurement. On the second photo that I took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before you go to the most recent one, can we get your agreement that it is between those marks that you've put that you have measured the 15.2 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the discussion, I was taking a look, and giving it some thought, to look at the diagram again. The point I took is the dome of the heel to have an exactitude here. We measured the top and the bottom. That's how we measured it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Doctor, I'm sorry to interrupt you but that diagram clearly, where it shows 15.2 centimetres, is not showing the length of the fracture. That's what's got me worried. And I thought that you had said that those figures had slipped in some way. What I want you to do is to show us on the X-ray where you get this figure of 15.2 centimetres from. Do you see my problem? You've got 15.2 centimetres from what you call the dome. Now, nobody suggests, do they, that the fracture started down at the dome, so where do you get this figure of 15.2 centimetres from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at the diascope on which the X-rays are placed, if you do that, then we place a line or a thread and we are able to measure in this way. That is how we measure distance on bones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Doctor, I'll only ask you once more and after that I'm going to give up. You will see in the diagram that you have a figure of 15.2 centimetres which is measured from what you have described as the dome of the bone. Now that clearly is not where the fracture started. You also told us that the figures in that diagram had somehow slipped. Now, what I am trying to find out from you, and it seems to me such a simple question, how do you measure the length of the fracture as 15.2 centimetres when you look at the X-ray?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just saying that we take the dome, a point which is fixed, that has nothing to do with the thing we are examining, and we take a thread, a horizontal line, in fact, and from that horizontal line we take a measurement and we read the superior point that we find. And we can't go beyond that point in another direction. So the superior point is marked by -- is hidden by the bone but nevertheless we try to find the superior point on all the X-rays of the same object taken at the same time, and so it is a point which I indicated here and we look at the -- try and find the inferior point, the lowest point. This is a more certain point here. We have this horizontal here, and we mark that point and then measure. That is how we measure fractures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, doctor, then it wasn't, if I may suggest to you, a fracture that was 15.2 centimetres long. It was a fracture which started at a point 15.2 centimetres above the dome and which may have ended at 8.4 centimetres above the dome. So that the horizontal difference between the two was 6.8 centimetres. It's not the length of the fracture. It's just that the fracture commences 6.8 centimetres horizontally above.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the 1992 one. Now, is the exercise on the left-hand side, the 2001 measurements, so that the highest point of the fracture is 20.3 centimetres above the dome and the lowest point is 3.9 centimetres above the dome, so there is a horizontal difference of 16.4 centimetres? Now, is that what we are dealing with? Are those the differences you see? No good just nodding. It won't be in the transcript. Are you agreeing with me?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [English] 200 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, I think I can understand it, Mr. Groome. I'm sorry, the doctor had told us about the difference in lengths. I hope I have explained to myself what it is the doctor is referring to. It's a horizontal difference of 6.8 centimetres for the 1992 fracture, and it's a horizontal difference of 16.4 centimetres for the 2001 X-ray shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, if I may take it just one step further, if we subtract 16.4 -- if we subtract 6.8 centimetres from 16.4 centimetres, we end up with a difference of 9.2 centimetres between the uppermost portion and the lowermost portion of these fractures; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In a horizontal plane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a horizontal plane?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Well, you are now comparing potatoes and other vegetables. We can discuss measurements and planes if it is the same victim, but there are other elements that tell us that this is not the same person. So if we are discussing a length, the principle is, is it the same fracture, and the answer we have to say is yes or no, is it or isn't it? So I do apologise. I was really very troubled by the question about measurement, because I never thought of this. This question, in fact, is not one that we are disputing. When I look at the X-rays that I have here, I see different fractures. I'm still not speaking about two different people, but I'm speaking about two different fractures, the position, the strength and stress used. So I am looking at the diagrams and at the planes and I am -- the conclusion I have come to is that the fractures are of two different people. You led me astray through some of your questions but that doesn't matter. We get back to basics. I apologise for having to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Doctor, perhaps I should explain to you our respective functions in this case. The Prosecution has to demonstrate that there is no reasonable possibility that these are X-rays of the same person. And that decision as to whether they have proved that is ours. That's why I have been very anxious to find out from you what it is you're saying so that I can understand it. And you have demonstrated, along these lines, that the fractures are in entirely different places. That's the first thing. And the Prosecution, as I understand it, is going to take to you the heel bone, but before we go to the heel bone, is there anything else, when you compare these two X-rays, that has persuaded you that they are of different people?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, before we move to the heel structure, I'd like to ask one more question regarding the fractures we are now discussing at length, if I may, Your Honour. Doctor, earlier in your testimony you described the fracture indicated in the 1992 X-ray as a spiral fracture. Can you please characterise the fracture in the 2001 X-ray? Is that a spiral fracture?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe how somebody would incur the injury that you observed in the 2001 X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: I did not address that question in my report but I can answer it, or at least try to do so. The fracture that I find on the 1992 X-rays are fractures that can be called spiral. All tibia fractures are spiral. It is twisted. As I was saying a moment ago, among -- one finds such fractures in football players, skiers; it is a fracture caused by tortion. The fracture that I examined, the principal plane is one that goes from the front backwards. So if one is facing someone and you have a plank, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you can break the plank, and you have a fracture -- I need a piece of paper. You have a plank and a fracture like this. Then, it would be demonstrated in this way. And you see that it is like something has slipped. The fracture that I have before me from 1992 is a fracture one comes across, a pedestrian who is hit by a car in a traffic accident. Or as a pedestrian, so this is a fracture which is due to external influence. The leg is folded or -- excuse me, I have to get up. Leg moves forward. I hope I have managed to demonstrate. If you are hit from the front, the leg is going to be raised and you have a fracture like this. It has different characteristics therefore, compared to those in the first X-ray.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before you ask another question, I think we better clear something up in the transcript. The one you're talking about, about the pedestrian being hit by a car in a traffic accident, is that the 1992 or the 2001 X-ray?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. There is just a reference to 1992. It may be a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, doctor, would it be fair to say that the two fractures are of different types and caused by different mechanisms?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, did you also compare the structure of the heel of the two X-rays, the X-rays taken in August 2001 and the 1992 X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: In 1992, here are the details. We see the heel, which is pointed, and what I found here, it is rounded. One could say there was arthrosis but if there were arthrosis then this one should be pointed and not rounded because with aging--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Wait a minute, doctor. What page of your report are you pointing to there? Is it page 17 or page 18?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 18, page 18. The same photograph can be found on another page too. No?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just work with one photograph at a time, doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And these are the 2001 again, are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2001. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender page 18 into evidence as 21.4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P21.4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, I would ask you to go step by step and ask you to indicate certain things on the X-rays that are now before us. I would ask you just to work with the documents. Please do not put anything else on the ELMO at this time. Doctor, I'd ask you to circle the portion of the heel structure on the 1992 X-ray that you observed or you examined. Can you circle the portion or the area that you examined? On the 1992 X-ray? On the 1992 X-ray?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: On the 1992 X-ray, doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, doctor, just the 1992 X-ray. Can you describe -- I see you've drawn a line now to indicate a portion of the 1992 X-ray. Can you please describe for us the shape of that structure? Just the 1992 X-ray.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: It is pointed here. The lowest point of the calcaneum, as we call it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've also drawn a line to indicate the same structure on the 2001 X-ray. I'd ask you to now describe how the -- how the structure appears in the 2001 X-ray.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: This point here is rounded, this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, after examining the X-ray from -- purported to be from 1992 and those that you were involved in taking in August of 2001, are you able to say with a degree of scientific certainty whether or not they are of the same person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you talking only of the heel at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, of the two sets of X-rays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, scientific certainty is not the test we are dealing with. You have to persuade us that they could not reasonably be the same person. Now, I know doctors and lawyers have this problem throughout, but that's the test. And scientific certainty doesn't mean a thing from a lawyer's point of view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, after examining or comparing the X-rays from 1992 with those that you were involved in taken in August of 2001, are you able to say whether or not these two -- the people or the bones depicted in both of these X-rays could not reasonably be of the same person?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: These are not the same persons, but not only relying on this point. There are different points. We cannot rely on a single point. That would be dangerous. One particular point can be due to the way in which an X-ray was taken. But here, there is difference over here, up here, different talus and other points that cannot be found. So it's not just one point but several points that differ. For example, I haven't written it in my report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we take them one by one? You've shown us the point of the heel. That's the first one. Now, what's your next point? Let's take them one by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there another structure on the two heels that is not similar? One by one, doctor.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: This is the first. Here above, it can't quite be seen on the reproduction but I have the originals over here. This too is extremely pointed and on the second take, in August 2001, it is rounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I'd ask you to put the number 2 next to those two structures you're now referring to.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there other structures that you can observe in the comparison of these two X-rays that are different?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: I should like to assist by saying that I took the heel several times. There are small differences in angle, to make sure I'm not mistaken. So we tried to test ourselves, and that is why here we have a point three, a kind of hole in the talus, which one can not find on the other. On any of these other X-rays. One could not find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you found a hole in the talus of the 1992 X-ray that you did not find in the 2001 X-ray; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any other differences in the heel structure?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just before we go on, is that hole you're referring to, the one that you thought might have been relevant to traction, where traction has been applied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In your report, your most recent report, you referred to a hole that you had seen or some mark on the heel, I've forgotten which, which you said was consistent with there having been traction applied. Is this the hole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Here I shall mark it with a number 4. That is the trace of traction, which is not found on this other X-ray. I should also like to make an observation. You have here the same heel but the way in which the X-ray was taken differed slightly, and you see here that there is no rounding, but you could say it depends on the X-ray. This was an X-ray taken shortly after the X-ray so there was no traction. This was taken later. Secondly. Traction is achieved by attachment to the bone for days and the human body reacts by calculosis, calcification, which prevents the -- this is known as the fire well, a kind of envelope of the bone and we see that here, but not over here. So this could not have been due to traction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But the hole, the number 4 that you've shown, you think that that was consistent with traction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But the absence of that hole on the 1992 X-ray would not be significant, I suggest, because the X-ray is usually taken before the traction is applied. That's so, is it not? It's a matter of ordinary orthopaedic practice. You're nodding. I'm sorry, doctor, but it has to be recorded in the transcript. But the point, you still haven't said yes. Are you not able to say it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot put it better than Mr. President, Your Honour, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that compliment. I just want to make sure it's recorded somewhere. And whilst we are on this question of traction, may I ask you what is really an orthopaedic question? Is it usual for there to be traction applied if only the tibia is broken and not both bones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what I thought about seeing the traction in our area. In the western countries, traction is not applied. We have various other means. Traction is applied in situations of war or poverty or lack of surgical resources. Not only the shortage of surgical equipment but also medicines, because any intervention on the skeleton, surgery, is -- opens the possibility of infection and osteomyelitis. And anyone familiar with bone diseases knows that once you get osteomyelitis once and one can never tell when it can be treated. Shortage of antibiotics, medical materials, all this leads -- encourages traction. Another minor detail that is not to be found in my report is the position of the traction is uncustomary in our area because traction is one centimetre too high and too much forward. If in our areas we were to apply such traction, there is the risk of affecting the nerves and the tendons and the arteries that are to be found here, and so it is very risky. And if anyone did this in this particular position, it must have been a doctor with an enormous amount of experience. I immediately thought of Jozsef Trueta [phoen], the orthopaedic surgeon of the antifascist forces in the civil war in Spain. He became a professor of orthopaedics at London University. He would be somebody who could do this. The doctor who treated Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic in Serbia is a really great doctor with a capital D. It is strange that a little mark like this can lead to observations of this kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But, doctor, equally it could have been in times of stress or war and by a doctor who didn't quite know what he was doing. Is that not reasonably possible? I'm trying to reduce this case to what are the real issues, you see. Is it reasonably possible that a doctor without having served in the civil law -- civil war with the colleague you refer to, has made perhaps a bad error of judgement, but is it reasonably possible that it was put there for the purposes of traction? And that it did not need to be a fracture of both bones because in the circumstances they may not have had metal pins or anything like that available to them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. If there is a fracture of one bone, one would avoid intervening even with a needle. If there is a fracture of two bones, if possible, it needs to be treated surgically with a cushion of nail or a platelet. There is no reason to put a needle unless two bones are broken. The fact that a needle was put was because they were obliged to apply traction. As I was saying, due to lack of material and also because this was necessary, because of the nature of the fracture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. We will, now -- Mr. Groome, you want to start something knew?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Maybe just finish up this area before the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, taking the totality of the all the comparisons that you made of the tibia, of the fibula, and the heel structures of the bone, are you able to render us an opinion whether or not the leg of the 1992 X-ray and that of Mr. Vasiljevic taken in August of 2001, could they reasonably be the same person?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: No. They were not of the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The test, I'm sorry to correct you, Mr. Groome, is it reasonably possible that they were the same person?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the test.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it reasonably possible that they are of the same person?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, doctor. May I suggest this is a place to pause?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. We will resume again at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, in addition to what you've testified to earlier today, did your examination of the 1992 X-ray indicate some irregularities regarding the labelling of that X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: What I was struck by was that the identification was written in handwriting on that X-ray. There was a label, a sticker, which was stuck to the X-rays. Is that what you wanted to ask me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in addition to that, were there other indications on or in the labelling portion of the X-ray that you found irregular?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: The irregularity -- I'm struck by the irregularities afterwards, after the study and after having made my conclusions that it was an X-ray -- X-rays of two different people. After that, I looked at the other differences, but let me repeat, I am a physician and what I'm interested in first and foremost are the medical aspects. Everything else is -- are the technical aspects, which, in principle, do not come under my realm of expertise. I am not qualified to give opinion on those technicalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to the bottom of the X-ray and there are several white boxes or the outlines of white boxes. Do you know which boxes I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: I have paid attention to that part. I speak about that part in my first report where I speak about the identification of the document. It is customary that documents are described in a certain way, standard procedure. On the first document, I mention something that I noticed. This is the detail and I have photographed that detail. What do we see here? If we look at this bottom half here, let me make a sketch to make what I want to say clearer. What we can see on the back, this sticker covers another sticker, and when you take a closer look at this, which I did and photographed, here it is, you gain the impression that a piece of paper has been stuck over the X-ray and as it was not exactly superimposed, you can see the traces of the sticky material. If I were to take a piece of paper like this, for example, and fold it over so, you see? Then I take another piece of paper and put it inside between the folds. You can see that this has been folded. But as I say, these are just details that one can notice, but it is not up to me to explain them, to give them an explanation of how they got there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your experience as somebody who has examined numerous X-rays, would this be something that you would expect to find on an X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Well, every X-ray has some form of identification. Here we can see the name of the person, the person who requested the X-ray, and the date. This is either prepared before the actual X-ray is taken or it is placed on the X-ray afterwards. So it contains usually the name of the patient, the date the X-ray was taken and the author of the X-ray, the person who took the X-ray. Which I can't find here. This has been written in handwriting, we see a date here, and it is not a very legible piece of writing, and on the basis of that, we don't know who took the X-ray.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I'd ask you --

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Whether it was some sort of spirit or who actually took it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- to just with your pen circle the areas which appear to you to be other labels placed on this X-ray. Would you just circle those areas that indicate that to you?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Well, this has been stuck on, and there was -- it was superimposed. I can -- by looking at this, I can count three stickers, and if you take a closer look, and have the X-ray in your hands, there is a sticker that starts here and ends there, and then you have another sticker that begins -- here it is, not very visible. You can only barely make it out. But in my opinion, that is another sticker. And somebody tried to place the sticker on several times. I don't know actually what happened but it's not standard procedure. What is usually done is one sticker is stuck on and that's it, that's the end of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I'd ask to you put a number 1 next to the first sticker that you see on the bottom of this X-ray, just to indicate which one -- where that is. Just, not on the X-ray itself, doctor, on the exhibit that's on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: No, no. I can't say which sticker was the first and which was stuck on subsequently. I don't know. I can't say that. But I can see three stickers. I don't know which came first. I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to tell us which came first. Can you put the numbers 1, 2 and 3 next to the three different labels that you see evidence of on the X-ray?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Before I do that, in my first report, you have a detail here, and you can see the arrows marking those stickers. So there you have your answer. You have the arrows, 1, 2, 3, perhaps even four stickers. So you have it marked on that page. I can repeat what I did but you already have it on my report, page 3 of the first report. You have the arrows indicating the different stickers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to just repeat those markings on the exhibit that's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Shall I place a number 1 or 5, 6?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Number 1, 2, and 3 to indicate the three different labels that you see.

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, doctor. Now, during the course of your examination of Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic, did you interview him regarding how he injured his leg?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you summarise for us how it was he told you he injured his leg?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Well, I asked him how he had injured his leg, and I also asked him to reproduce the position he was in. And he was on the examining table in order to demonstrate this to me. He said that he had fallen to the ground and that he was on his right -- left-hand side, left-hand side, and that his right leg was behind him, according to what he said, and his left leg was a little to the front. Now, in that position, a horse would have fallen on his leg. So in this way, the inferior, internal leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say that a horse did fall on his leg?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the injuries that you --

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: I didn't ask him but he volunteered the information. He said that there was a horse which fell on his leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The injuries that you observed in the X-ray, the 2001 X-ray, were they consistent with his description of how he received a broken leg?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: If it occurred on a terrain which was not an even one, on a rougher terrain, then I would say that the explanation he gave me is consistent with the fracture that I myself observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would the fractures that you observed in the 2001 X-ray also be consistent with somebody slipping and falling on a steep, grassy embankment?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness now be shown Prosecution document number 62, a translation of the medical history form which is already in evidence as P138.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender Prosecution document number 62 a translation of an already -- an exhibit that's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The Exhibit 138 was the English translation -- the Serbian language one, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I thought this went in with it. I've seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I do not believe it did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Have you any objection to this, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be Exhibit P62.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, Exhibit number 62 you've had an opportunity to see this document already, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you are observations regarding the injury that you could see on the X-ray that -- the 2001 X-ray, are they consistent with the diagnosis indicated on lines 10 and 11 on this medical history form?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps you could translate them for us, doctor. Ten is a fracture of the tibia and something else. It's in Latin, you see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Point 10, in the left-hand column, in totality the tibular fractures are tibular, that is to say, it is the big bone. And the fine bone on the left-hand side. I think there has been a typing error. It says tibia but it should be fibula. So this typist seems to have made a typing error just like our own typists do from time to time. There are some other things too. Psychosis and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You were referred to number 11, though, number 10 and number 11. What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's in Latin. It is Latin of the middle ages. They are expressions that we don't use. We haven't been using them since the 1950s, but fractura cruris is the lower leg. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. But this is really ancient Latin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And what is the 1 sin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did you say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Number 10 and number 11 have the figure 1 and then the abbreviation, SIN. Is that another Latin expression?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Fen? Sinistra, sinistra, left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. You think they have given the diagnosis of a fracture of the tibia and the fibula; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Both legs. Both legs have been marked as being fractured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Both legs or both bones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bones. It's a fracture of the left leg, two bones there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And this would have been filled in, would it not, after the X-rays?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. I can't say. Perhaps it was filled in before and afterwards. It is customary in an emergency unit, is that the patient is brought in and a nurse taking the X-rays places the X-rays at the disposal of the doctors. And to take an X-ray, on an average you need 1 minute 20 seconds. You get the X-rays after a minute and 20 seconds have gone by so that the doctor, the specialist, will -- waits for the X-rays because he can get such a speedy answer. So there is no need for him to do anything before he gets the X-rays. So I think, it is my opinion, that the X-rays were taken first and this was filled in afterwards because it is a speedy process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I want to draw your attention to line number 20. Does this form indicate the date and the time that the person sustained their injury?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: That is something that I also noticed. I remarked that too. And I was a Lieutenant Colonel in the Belgian army, the reserve forces, let us not forget that, so I do have some knowledge as to procedure with respect to accidents in wartime. And it is almost an obligation to fill in not only the date but the time, the hour and minute, and specific circumstances under which a lesion has occurred. The reason is a very simple one and that is that the wounded, anybody who has been injured at the end of a battle, resort to administration and the funds of the army to be remunerated for the injuries sustained. They might seek their pension rights. So if anybody asks for remuneration from the army, the army tries to avoid having to pay out anything it need not. So they are very meticulous in recording everything, in the administrative sense. And the medical staff too have to fill this in so that they always have proof of what the victim has sustained and that the situation corresponds to a battle situation where the injuries occurred. That is why the date and the hour and time is always introduced on all documents. And it usually is on the left-hand side. You have the MP, military post number, and case history and everything else. So this is a document which is a medical and military document. But this document is not a complete one, but it is an essential data bank for these purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date an hour of injury were left blank on this document; is that correct? Did you answer yes?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [English] Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would it be standard medical practice during the initial interview or initial examination of an injured person to ask them how they received their injury, assuming that the person was conscious at the time?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Certainly. We have to ask what the conditions were and normally, there would have to be at least two witnesses. From time to time we accept having just one witness. But we do have to have the testimony of somebody, of an eye witness, to the accident, in order to complete the dossier, the file. If we have no eye witnesses, well it becomes more difficult, so we have to avoid that. So in order to know when we have a valid witness, we have to have the time at which the accident took place, for example, at 10.00. And if you ask the witness, "Where were you at that particular time?" That is the technique we use, the administrative techniques. So I am answering -- my answer is yes normally, but there are situations where this doesn't always meet the regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the patient is conscious, wouldn't the doctor interview the patient and ask the patient him or herself how it was they were injured?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: It depends. We -- if we have nothing else to do, if the -- then we spend a little time asking the patient. This will depend on the assistants, because doctors are always very busy, busy. If they have other victims, they are not going to waste their time interviewing the person who has received the injury. It's usually up to the nurses, and of course the doctor is usually not alone. He always has his assistants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to the third page of this exhibit and ask you to read aloud the first paragraph of a note by Dr. Jovicevic?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it out in French or in English?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if you don't mind if you read this portion in English as that is what we have before us?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: [English] "Admit to the ward as an emergency case, because of a simple fracture of the left tibia caused by a fall on a flat surface in the battlefield. Did not lose consciousness. On admission, the tibia was deformed. Movement pathological. Active movement not possible. Passive movement painful and restricted."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, doctor. During your examination of the medical history form in this case, did you find any reference to a horse or an accident involving a horse?

utterances.speaker: YVAN DE GRAVE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet? Cross-examined by Mr. Domazet:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
