utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, she mentioned VG1 -- 101, VG78 and VG999 as being -- as dying in the fire on Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did she identify them by the name that they had or used at that time?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: She did. VG13 identified the three of them by the name that they had in 1992, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did she identify, did she identify them both as sisters?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just to clear up some confusion, I draw your attention to VG79. Are there two individuals connected with this case that have the same name?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without telling us who they are, we'll leave it to the Court to figure that out. During the course of your investigation, did you become aware that Mr. Vasiljevic had represented himself to be some type much official or have some official relationship with the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you investigate that aspect of the case?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours. What the investigation team did at the time when we learned that some of our witnesses were saying that Mr. Vasiljevic represented himself as being a representative for the ICRC International Community for the Red Cross, we sent an official request to their representative in Geneva to inquire if Mr. Vasiljevic was ever a member of the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive a reply?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that reply indicate?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: That Mr. Vasiljevic was at no time a representative of the ICRC in Geneva working anywhere in Bosnia or former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I Would ask at this time that the witness be shown Prosecution document 51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You should have that framed in a golden frame. It must be the first time the ICRC has ever sent anything, at least in writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Investigator Roy, do you recognise what Exhibit 51 is?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: This is the response to the request that we sent to the Committee International de la Croix Rouge, ICRC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection to it being entered as Exhibit P51, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you it will be Exhibit P51.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Investigator Roy, did you also attempt to contact governmental authorities of the Republika Srpska to ascertain whether he represented any local branch of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you in fact attempt to ascertain whether he had any type of official position for refugees or otherwise with the government of the Republika Srpska during the time period concerned in this case?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, did you also make inquiry into the existence of any criminal record for Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours. It was on the same request.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time I would ask that the witness be shown Prosecution document number 69 and 69.1, 69 being the English translation of 69.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Investigator Roy, I'd ask to you look at Prosecution document number 69. Do you recognise what it is?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. It's the translation of the response from the Republika Srpska government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it indicate whether or not Mr. Vasiljevic held any type of position with the Red Cross, the local red cross in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, it does, that Mr. Vasiljevic was never a member of the Red Cross of any humanitarian representative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it indicate whether or not he had any position of appointment by the government of the Republika Srpska to any official duties in the time period concerned in this case?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. They say that Republika Srpska authority did not appoint him to any official duty for their government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour at this time I would tender Prosecution documents number 69 and 69.1 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you they will be Exhibits P69 and P69.1. You do not need to get the witness to read out bits or confirm them. We can read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were involved in taking a statement from Mr. Vasiljevic in the matters concerned with this case?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honour, on the 16th and 17 of November 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Vasiljevic make any statement to you regarding any activity or anything he did after the killing of the man at the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Look, we've already got this in evidence. We've got the video in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Let's get on with it. Let's not double check anything. There was no objection to any of it. Then let's get on with what you have to prove from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: To understand the next question, Your Honour, I would need an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right, go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this way, Investigator Roy: Did there come a time when you investigated whether or not Mr. Vasiljevic went to the police station and filed a report claiming that Milan Lukic had committed murder at the Drina River on the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I did send a request to the Republika Srpska government asking them for the report that Mr. Groome mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any record of any criminal report being filed by anybody against Milan Lukic during the time period that we are concerned with?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely none, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would now ask the witness be shown Prosecution documents 162 and 163. 163 being the original and 162 being the English translation of that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Investigator Roy, I'd ask to you take a look at Exhibit number 162 and 163. Do you recognise what they are?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely. The original version from the government of Republika Srpska and our official translator here at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there also come a time during the course of this investigation that you attempted to investigate whether or not Mr. Vasiljevic was a member of the Territorial Defence of the military and whether or not he was injured in performance of those duties?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do to investigate this aspect of his account?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: On the 5th of April of this year, I sent a request to the Republika Srpska government inquiring about the military files of Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic. His time of mobilisation, if he was injured during the war, everything relating to military aspects. Since the sending of my request, I never have any answer, never received any answer from the Republika Srpska government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, this document, 162, doesn't tie up in any way. What does file 06-01/94 deal with? This is, as I understand it, an attempt to check whether he went to the police station and spoke to a subsequently deceased police officer to report what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, where do we see that here?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This letter states that after checking the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I've read it and it talks about a file number 06-01/94 not existing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is the file related to incidents involving Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. File 06-01/94 for all we might know might relate to a robbery of the local corner store.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, it says, Your Honour, after that related to incidents involving Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. It still doesn't tie it in with what the accused said during the course of his interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will find the request, the specific request and enter that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think you'll have to to make any sense of that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, so that we do not delay, I will have the actual request brought down and perhaps on my re-examination, after cross, I can enter that in through the investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, subject to cross-examination, but any way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be shown Exhibit number 64, Prosecution document 64.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Investigator Roy, do you recognise what Prosecution document number 64 is?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. It's the request that I sent on the 5th of April 2001 to the RS government inquiring about military files for Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I have no further questions of the investigator. Will Mr. Domazet agree to permit me to inquire about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What are you going to do with this? Was there ever any reply might be an important thing to make it admissible?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, Your Honour. Prosecution tenders the Prosecution document number 64 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But we still don't know whether there was any reply to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Investigator Roy, was there ever any reply to that request?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: There was never a reply, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objection to the document marked 64 Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be Exhibit P64.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will now conclude my examination if Mr. Domazet agrees I may inquire about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we will give you leave to do it later on any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet. Cross-examined by Mr. Domazet:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Roy, do you remember investigating this case in the course of this year, having had a conversation with a person of Muslim ethnicity, who was a patient at the Uzice hospital in May, June and July 1992, in connection with Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't like to mention his name, at least not at this stage. I think he has the pseudonym VG113, and could the witness be shown the list to confirm whether that is the witness in question?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: The name of the witness is not on the list that I've got here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, it's true. You have another other list?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: The name of the witness is not on this list either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you like to write out a special piece of paper, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You have not yet sought protective measures so far as I'm aware so we haven't given you any numbers yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But I'm sure that this witness had his -- I think that he is 113.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You write his name out and show it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: If you're telling me, Mr. Domazet, that this name is 113, I'll go along with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But is that name on that piece of paper the witness that you spoke to or the person you spoke to and whose name was subsequently given to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Now we will mark that as a document under Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. seal for you. It will be Exhibit D5 and it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Roy, do you remember this person giving you some documents? The discharge, his discharge paper, from that hospital, as evidence as to the time he spent in hospital?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: If I recall, Your Honour, I've seen documents and I made a photocopy of the documents. They should be with this VG113 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean the person whose name was on that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Because he may not turn out to be 113?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Well, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have here this statement in English and in B/C/S, and it says on it, that the witness is 113. But that witness hasn't been called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Let's not worry about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall showing to that person this photo spread which you also showed to other witnesses as you just explained to us?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: I would have to refer to the statement. Usually it's written in the statement if we show a photo spread or photo array of someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In the statement, it says that it was shown to him, and that he identified Mitar Vasiljevic as person number 9 and signed it.

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it could be. I have to see if my signature is on it, on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you got it there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Show it to him, please.

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, my signature is on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Roy, that this person confirmed that Mitar Vasiljevic was in the Uzice hospital at the same time as he was there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's hearsay, Your Honour, and it's an available witness that could be called to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure what weight we would give to it, Mr. Domazet. It's a matter for you. If you want to secure his credit in advance, that's one thing, I suppose, to save Mr. Roy being recalled, but it's certainly nothing that's going to be given any weight as evidence of the facts stated. You've got the witness to be called. You were given access to him. And as I understood from something that was said during the Pre-Trial Conference or it might have been in your pre-trial brief, you are going to call him. So I don't know what the purpose of getting this evidence in is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid that this witness may not come at the request of the Defence and in my view, he is a very important witness, but if there are objections of this kind, I shall simply try and tender this discharge document into evidence, given by the witness, which I have had translated into English and I have sufficient copies of it. But we shall try to bring this witness as a Defence witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we are talking about the same thing. When you say a discharge document, do you mean your client's discharge document or your prospective witness's discharge document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Potential witness, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you can do that. That's not hearsay. It's just a means of proving it, but if you have some concerns about being able to get the witness, then hearsay may have some weight. But you would have to establish why you are unable to call the witness. Mr. Groome, I hesitate to let in unnecessary evidence in, but if there is a problem, we then have to get Mr. Roy back again to prove the statement that was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Roy works in the building and would be available any time Mr. Domazet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He wasn't last week, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, other than an emergency he would be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That lovely phrase that the OTP uses, "he may be on mission," but if that's so, then we can recall him. Well, Mr. Domazet, may I suggest you tender your prospective witness's discharge document if this witness is able to identify it in some way. Otherwise you'll have to get it in some way later on if your witness does not come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I agree, Your Honour. And I would like to ask the witness to look at it. He did examine the whole statement taken, to which this document is attached, and I am also submitting it in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What I suggest is that you tender the discharge summary, because that's original evidence, and we'll have the statement which this witness is able to identify marked for identification. And then it may then be proved without having to recall Mr. Roy. What do you say to that, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would agree to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We have no pseudonym for him yet. Shall we call him Witness D1? Or that may be confused with exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, yes, why not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How about VGD1? We will call him VGD1 for the moment and his discharge summary will be D6, and the statement that you say the witness took from him, that will be marked for identification 1. And then that won't be in evidence but at least it will be proved without having to recall Mr. Roy if it becomes necessary. Yes. You proceed. You better get the documents admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] May I give this document to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The B/C/S original is the one that was attached to the statement. First time I see the translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is the other document the statement which you took from this witness who we will call VGD1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's only a photocopy of his release paper. If I look at the translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you haven't not got it yet. The usher will pick it up for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this is the statement that I took from VG13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Or VGD1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: VGD1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Domazet, you proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Roy, do you recall that this witness handed over to you or told you that he had given a written statement to the police in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: I recall, Your Honours, that this witness did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recollect roughly when that statement was given, in relation to the time when you took your statement?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: If I recall, Your Honours, I think it was in 1997, but I have to look at the document. I've seen the document before, but I would have to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you got it there, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, show it to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it was taken in 1997, the 7 of June 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question: As the investigator, Mr. Roy, did you talk to a Muslim woman who eye-witnessed Mitar Vasiljevic's fall from a horse?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I only have her name but not her pseudonym, so perhaps I should write it down too, to remind the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And then write beside it VGD2, would you?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that document will be Exhibit D7 and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour, and if I understood you correctly, it is not necessary for me to provide several copies, because we have to wait to see whether these documents will be admitted or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the real documents, if I may so describe them, the two reports, have become part of the evidence, but the statement by the witness has not. That's the statement to the investigator. Yes, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just one question of the witness, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet has just asked you about whether you interviewed a woman who stated that she observed Mr. Vasiljevic fall off a horse. Did this woman tell you the date on which she observed this?

utterances.speaker: Yves Roy
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It was between the 22nd and the 24th of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your task is finished. You're free to leave. Thank you for coming to give your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Now, you've got some 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Ms. Bauer will take care of the introduction of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you recollect, we took up your suggestion to mark the binders and with a sort of -- to make a decision on what portions of the statements the Prosecution intends to rely. We undertook that. We have multiplied all the binders. They are here and ready. We have undertook also another exercise. We redacted some names of protected witnesses in both the English and the B/C/S version, and in addition, we took out some English versions of statements that seemed not to be relevant to that case. In the B/C/S version, I have to add, since it was the original version, this certified statements were taken, I just put a note in, "Irrelevant," because I didn't want to tear those original certified statements apart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Those names you've redacted, the names themselves have been made known to the defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I would say the names were known throughout the proceedings. They were protected witnesses throughout the proceedings and they are referred to with their pseudonyms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: And we marked the binder as document number 143.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How many statements are in there?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Six statements, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps you could just read the names or pseudonyms of them on to the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: They were not protected witnesses, so I think I can read the names out for the record. It is a statement of Simeon Vasic, including the affidavit provided in the United States. It is Fikret Cocalic, (redacted), Mehmet Tabakovic, and Mehmet Turkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You'll do a kindness if you give those names to the Court reporters. Any objection to those, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, except for what I already stated, and that is that my only objection was that witness -- regarding witness Simeon Vasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Remind me. I remember you raising an issue about one of them. You put some documents in in response, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I relied on the documents attached to his statement, in fact, in which it was stated that at the time he had been mobilised and was a member of the army for the period when he says he worked at the dam and that he received orders about the release of the water from the dam. I do not have any evidence here to say that he never held that position, because I have not been able to get hold of that document, but I might be able to do that subsequently. However, I thought this witness should not be heard under Rule 92 bis. As for all the others, I had no objection and I have no objection now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Under which part of the Rule 92 bis do you say he does not qualify?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you referring to the statement of the witness, the part of the statement that I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm worried about the formalities of Rule 92 bis, first of all. Now, does the evidence, or the material in it, do other than go to proof of a matter other than the acts and conduct of the accused as charged in the indictment? That's the first qualification that has to be satisfied. In other words, does it deal at all with the facts relating to your client's conduct as alleged in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. My client is not mentioned at all in his statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- in any way whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And it deals mainly with the alleged attack upon the civilian population by the look of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: About which there has been no substantial issue taken. The declaration that is attached to it, a notary public is certainly a person who is authorised to witness statements in accordance with the law and procedure of any state, even the United States. The declaration seems to satisfy the terms of the rule. So the only issue is whether it goes in in whole -- the statement goes in in whole or in part and whether he is required to appear for cross-examination. Now, you want to challenge one of the statements in it, as I understand it, because you say you have some document to prove that he, as I recall you said, did not hold the office which he says that he holds inside the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, because in his statement, he says that he was employed at the hydro power plant and that he received orders from the municipal staff from the autumn of 1992 until October 1993 and he has attached a certificate of the command of the second Podrinje Brigade showing that he was engaged in a unit of that brigade of the army of Republika Srpska, from the 9th of May 1992 to the 16th of September 1993. As far as regards the certification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Wait a moment. I see no certificate attached to the statement at all. Are we talking with the same person Simeon Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have his number 6613524.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that's not the number I've got on mine. He says, according to the statement that I have, that he started working at the hydro plant at Visegrad in 1985. He worked as a supervisor. He was the only Serb in the office. Whereabouts in the statement is there about receiving instructions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the document I have received, it is to be found on page 645516, in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see. Now, you want to challenge that he was employed at the hydro plant at that time, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because he has provided a certificate showing that he was in the army at the time, and even when he was employed at the power plant, he did not hold such a position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Who has provided the certificate? Mr Vasic himself, has he?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume so, because I received it from the Prosecution in the binder of exhibits attached to his statement, together with some other written documents which he probably provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, none of those have been tendered. What's the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am unaware of the certificate. I would agree that if Mr. Domazet shows us the certificate and it is a certificate that was connected with the statement, that I would agree that it be introduced as a Defence exhibit on the Defence case. I'm not in possession of the certificate at the moment and I am unaware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, Mr. Domazet, is that the only challenge that you wanted to put to this person if he had been called as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if we were to call him as a witness, we would have things to ask him, although the individual never mentioned Mitar Vasiljevic anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if I can be of assistance, if that is a problem, then perhaps not to make it a problem, I can withdraw my objection and exclude that as a piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I do not want you to withdraw any of your objections or your client's rights. The whole purpose of Rule 92 bis is to reduce the time taken by giving the evidence. There is at the very end of the Rule a provision that the Trial Chamber may decide whether a part of the transcript can be rejected or whether to require the witness to appear for cross-examination. In general, you will not get a ruling from the Trial Chamber that a person should attend unless there is some real issue that you want to put to the witness. Now, if you would have put to the witness, had he been called as a witness, this certificate, which challenges a statement which he's made and which appears on the face of it to be relevant to the Prosecution case, we would have brought him along for cross-examination so you could do so. What Mr. Groome has offered is, well, he'll agree to you putting the statement in if you can show him that it's in some way associated with the statement. He appears to have no knowledge of its existence and I can assure you we have no knowledge of its existence. There is no reference to it in the statement itself, for example. May I suggest that you speak to Mr. Groome about this? We can deal with it informally if there is an agreement between you, in the morning. And I mean not in Court but there can be, if you write a consent to this being dealt with, we'll deal with it in the way which you've agreed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this certificate is in B/C/S. It wasn't translated. And that is why it was appended to this, so possibly that was the reason, that was why Mr. Groome was not aware of it. But I don't wish to insist upon this because one of my objections was precisely with respect to the certification of that statement, and at that time, I didn't have proof and evidence that in the -- his certificate was -- statement was certified, so I think -- and I don't think that the statement has any great bearing on the Mitar Vasiljevic case. So I would like to withdraw my objection and we can follow along Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you're satisfied with that, Mr. Domazet, you're a very experienced counsel and I wouldn't try to persuade you one way or the other. Very well, then, there is no objection to these documents going into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. But I would like to ask, if possible, in view of the fact that I'm not here tomorrow, if we have VG81 left over, some business left over, and if we could agree and harmonise our views, that is to say me and Mr. Groome, and that it be recorded in the transcript. There were several points that do not stand in the statement that Witness VG81 gave here in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is the one that you wanted to deal with yesterday? I'm sure that we can get an agreement about that. You want to have noted in the evidence that her statement did not contain a number of matters to which you referred to in her evidence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you can deal with that, can't you, and we can have that agreement noted at the Pre-Defence conference on Monday week?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that would be sufficient. There is one other matter related to this witness. If you recall, this witness refused to identify a number of people from the village of Kosovo Polje and the Court stated that it would credit her evidence less if she did not state those names. I spoke with her and I spoke with Mr. Domazet and offered to make those witnesses available for counsel to interview should he wish to do so and he has declined to do that. So I think that's important that the transcript reflect that those unnamed witnesses were made available to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean their names were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Their names and the Prosecution, not their names, Your Honour, the Prosecution offered to have those people to meet Defence or Defence investigator in the Sarajevo field office at a time convenient to the Defence, to further their investigation on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So that they would ascertain who -- what their identity was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. And what they could contribute to information about this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that can be noted. Is that the end of the bits and pieces, if I may so describe them?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to say not quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The folder of 92 bis witness statements will be Exhibit P143.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Prosecution and the Defence have agreed on some additional exhibits which have not been introduced throughout the trial, and we collected them. They are mainly official UN documentation or from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. UN organisations talking about Visegrad and also other parts of Bosnia and the persecution campaign in the form of widespread and systematic. There is one exhibit which probably I assume might shock in volume, which is the first exhibit, number P-- marked as number P5. Actually, the Prosecution would only intend to rely, and I can put this on the record, on pages 23 and 24 in the English translation of that document. So which would reduce the reading amount quite substantially, but we didn't want to tear apart the whole transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Were you going to take these one by one or globally.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I could simply read out the numbers and if Mr. Domazet has still an exhibit list, he could follow and simply say whether he would agree or object on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: And we have them globally put together in folders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. What's the next document?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: The first document would be P5. It's the minutes of the 12th session of the assembly of the Serbian people dated on the 24th March 1992. As outlined, we would only rely on the pages 23, 24 in the English version of that transcript, which is a decision on the verification of decision on the proclamation of newly established Serbian municipalities passed by the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P5, pages 23 and 24 only being relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: And the B/C/S translation of this exhibit is P5.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: P5.1, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: P6 is a telex message by the Assistant Minister of Internal Affairs of the Minister of Interior Internal Affairs of the Serbian Republic of BiH, dated the 31st of March 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Exhibit P6.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: 6.1 is again the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Exhibit P6.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Prosecution exhibit numbered 7 is a telex from the Visegrad Municipal Assembly declaring a state of emergency due to the deterioration of the political situation dated on the 6 April 1992. The B/C/S version is 7.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibits P7 and P7.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Next exhibit is only an English report, prenumbered document P12, a report by Tadeusz Mazowiecki on the situation of human rights in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and dated 10 February 1993. However, we only have certain passages relating to Bosnia, and not Croatia, Macedonia or any other parts of the former Yugoslavia in that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Exhibit P12.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Document marked prenumbered 13 is Council of Europe document, a report by Colin Kaizer on the war damages and cultural heritage in Croatia, BiH, dated 19th of January 1994, only related to the portions related to the municipality of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Exhibit P13.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Another report, document prenumbered 40, ICRC special report, the issue of missing persons in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia and Federal Republic of Yugoslavia by the ICRC in Geneva, done in Geneva, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Exhibit P40.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: The two final documents are P48, annex to the final report of the UN Commission of Experts, established pursuant to the Security Council resolution 780. In particular, the pages are 162 and -- to 165, dealing with the situation in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are those separate pages or all the pages between them?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Pages between them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wasn't quite able to find the page we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Pages 162 to 165 in the document numbered 48.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 162 to 168; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 162 to 165, according to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I gave away all my copies so I can't check whether I actually have -- that might be a typo on my list, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's only a three-page document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit P48.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: And the last number is prenumbered document 49, as well an annex to the final report of the UN Commission of Experts established pursuant to SC resolution 780, dated 27 May 1994, relating to activities of paramilitary forces in Bosnia, in particular the White Eagles, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, the UN commission report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P49.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That will conclude it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only remaining matter is the transcript of the accused's statement. There were some minor redactions and some minor corrections that Mr. Domazet and I have not yet had an opportunity to correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the only matter outstanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's the only matter outstanding. All the witnesses have been called and all the exhibits have now been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, will you be able to speak to Mr. Domazet about it before he goes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not sure we will be able to -- it's up to Mr. Domazet. I'm not sure that it's something that we can complete this evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, may I suggest this: That you close your case subject to that particular issue, and that at the Pre-Defence Conference on Monday the 22nd, I think it is, you can tender it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. That's acceptable to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you happy with that, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Domazet, as we indicated to you, we will require your compliance with Rule 65 ter paragraph (G), that's the list of witnesses and things, on or before Friday, the 19th of October. It can be faxed to us. The Pre-Defence Conference will be held on Monday morning, the 22nd of October. Hopefully that should not take long. The only matter I can see there should be any discussion about will be the attacks by Muslims upon the Serb civilian population. And then we would expect the Defence case to open on Tuesday, the 23rd of October. I remind you the Trial Chamber will not be sitting during the week of the 29th of October, but otherwise we will sit continuously, subject to any request by either of the parties for time out, or perhaps even a request by the Trial Chamber for time out if we are all exhausted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution at this time rests its case against Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Subject to that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Anything you want to raise, Mr. Domazet, before you go off to do your work?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, except to know hours of beginning on Monday 22, or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy to fit in with you because I don't think the conference should take long. Is 9.30 not convenient? I don't know what time the plane gets in from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I hope to be on Sunday here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, then, if we can start at 9.30 on Monday morning. We are very grateful to everyone concerned, the interpreters and the Court reporters and the Court staff, for sitting on. We will see you all here again on Monday, the 22nd of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 4.20 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
